vvb_guidance.quote_br_change: Beginning in late September 2026, AECN railcars are routed to a transload rail spur in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, instead of the rail yard at Opelousas, Louisiana. At Baton Rouge the oil is transferred from the railcar to tanker trucks and hauled by road to the injection site. The first transload at Baton Rouge took place on 22 September 2026.
vvb_guidance.quote_br_scope: In this Reporting Period, one railcar used the new route: SHPX215053, offloaded in Week 4 (INJ-09-2026-W4, 18 – 25 September 2026). Every other railcar in this Reporting Period was received at Opelousas under the existing routing.
vvb_guidance.quote_br_method: Each leg uses this railcar’s own mass and its own route distance, so the Opelousas distances are not applied to SHPX215053 and the Baton Rouge distances are not applied to any other railcar. The tanker leg is counted as a round trip, consistent with the treatment of the Opelousas leg.
vvb_guidance.quote_br_values: Rail distance from the loading origin to Baton Rouge: 2,152 (map evidence is added in drive). Tanker distance from Baton Rouge to the injection site: 136 mi one way, doubled for the round trip. Mass basis: the same scale-ticket net masses and loading Bill of Lading masses used for every other railcar.
vvb_guidance.quote_br_evidence: Week 4 ops notes, AECN Rail tab (Section 1 for the railcar’s route distances, Section 3 for the four offloads); certified truck scale tickets for each offload; loading Bills of Lading.
vvb_guidance.quote_loss_purpose: The difference is bio-oil that Charm received and transported but did not inject. Its upstream emissions, pyrolysis and transport from the loading origin to the rail yard, remain attributable to Charm and are reported on each AECN rail removal as a separate component, AECN Bio-oil Loss.
vvb_guidance.quote_loss_method: Pyrolysis and all transport components on the removal are calculated on the delivered mass: scale-ticket net mass, less any Uncertainty Adjustment. The lost mass, loaded mass minus delivered mass, is quantified per railcar and recognised in the week in which the railcar’s final offload is completed; a railcar that is still being offloaded carries no loss until it closes. Where a railcar’s scale tickets exceed its Bills of Lading, the excess is removed from the final offload through the Uncertainty Adjustment and the railcar’s loss is zero.
vvb_guidance.quote_loss_factor: Loss emissions apply the same AECN pyrolysis carbon intensities (process and embodied) and the same loading-origin-to-rail-yard transport emissions used for the delivered oil, pro-rated to the lost mass, which equates to approximately 0.229 t CO₂e per tonne of oil lost.
vvb_guidance.quote_loss_evidence: A platform-generated calculation record cannot yet be attached to each specific Certify datapoint; until it can, we have an example calculation attached to show the method.
